Macro-economic outlook 
Before we delve into the highlights of the quarter, I would like to share our perspective on the 
macroeconomic environment, particularly the volatility in the geopolitical arena and the impact of 
monsoon and El Nino on the rural economy, which remains an important consideration for the financial 
services industry in the current operating environment.

Global economy continues to be in a state of flux with re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia and 
sharp volatility in crude oil prices. At the same time, strong economic growth data combined with 
inflation pressures have reinforced expectations of higher-for-longer policy rates. 
While these uncertainties warrant close monitoring, India's domestic demand fundamentals and the 
underlying drivers of consumption continue to remain resilient. Input cost pressures have accentuated, 
but the pass-through has remained limited so far. Real GDP recorded a growth of 7.8% in Q1FY27, 
reflecting strong demand conditions on back of robust private consumption, investment and exports 
demand. Upgrades in India’s GDP growth expectations for the full year FY27 by RBI, World Bank, 
OECD etc underscore the strength of economic activity despite significant headwinds. Despite 
intermittent volatility in domestic financial markets, credit demand also continues to grow at robust pace.  
On the rural front, the progress of the southwest monsoon has remained an area of close attention for 
the entire financial services industry. As you would be aware, the 2026 Southwest monsoon concluded 
with cumulative rainfall at approximately 87% of the Long Period Average, with considerable regional 
variations. While rainfall improved during July, the deficit in the early part of the season and below-
normal rainfall in several regions have implications for agricultural output, water availability and rural 
cash flows. However, rainfall spells during the month of August have substantially improved the 
expectation of a near normal kharif outcome. 
Inspite of the below average monsoon, Kharif crop sowing is at par with previous years, reporting a 
marginal 1.0% YoY contraction with total coverage at 101% of the normal acreage. In most regions, 
irrigation buffer and stable reservoirs have helped mitigate rainfall shortfalls. While localised drop in 
crop yields and moderation in rural sentiments remain a latent risk, rural consumption continues to be 
strong currently, driven by resilient non-farm activities, robust govt DBT transfers and favourable terms 
of trade for agricultural prices. We are therefore maintaining a close watch on the operating environment 
across our rural markets, with particular attention to geographies where rainfall deficits and water 
availability could exert greater pressure on borrower cash flows. Sustained momentum in services, and 
broadly stable employment conditions are supporting urban demand as well. 
Despite cost pressures, manufacturing activities are holding well, as indicated by IIP and PMI figures 
and services sector activity remains steady and broad-based, owing to buoyant domestic and external 
demand. Economic momentum thus remains broad based and is expected to sustain strong demand 
through the current fiscal year. 
Q2FY27 Highlights 
Coming to this quarter’s highlights, I am pleased to share that L&T Finance has delivered another 
consistently strong quarter of profitable and quality-led growth. 
During Q2FY27, we recorded our highest-ever consolidated profit after tax of ₹975 Cr, representing a 
growth of 33% YoY, against ₹902 Cr in Q1FY27. Our consolidated book stands at ₹1,36,635 Cr, 
reflecting a YoY growth of 28%, against ₹1,29,634 Cr in Q1FY27, with an RoA of 2.60% against 2.48% 
in the previous quarter. This has been achieved on the back of quarterly Retail disbursements of 
₹24,027 Cr, up 27% YoY, with contributions from all our lines of business.

The disbursement momentum has been a result of our strong customer acquisition funnel, with a ~3 
crores customer database and our continued focus on granular distribution channels, branch footprint, 
digital acquisition capabilities, and our AI-powered credit administration framework, Project Cyclops, 
backed by strengthened risk guardrails. However, we consciously chose to attenuate our Rural 
disbursement momentum and raised risk guardrails in view of the uncertain progression of the 
monsoons. Now that we have reasonable clarity on the monsoon outcome, we will carefully increase 
our risk-calibrated rural disbursement momentum. 
You will remember that over the course of the last few calls, I have been emphasizing upon our 
trajectory of paring down credit cost on account of implementation of structural credit policy measures 
in our businesses and the implementation of Project Cyclops in various businesses. I am pleased to 
inform you that consequently, credit cost has moderated to 2.46% this quarter, reflecting a further 
sequential improvement of 8 bps from 2.54% in Q1FY27, supported by collections excellence and AI-
led portfolio management. We would like to reiterate that we are confident of achieving our guided credit 
cost corridor of 2%-2.2% by Q4FY27. Our NIMs + Fees, which is another focus area for us, stood stable 
at 10.48% against 10.47% in Q1FY27, well within our guided corridor of 10% to 10.5%. This was 
possible due to reduction in weighted average cost of borrowing achieved successfully through 
implementation of astute liability management. Opex remained range-bound at 4.08% during the 
quarter despite continued investments in branch-rollouts as well as technology investments. All of this 
has resulted in an improvement in our RoA to 2.60%, with RoE consequentially increasing to 13.56%. 
We remain hopeful that our RoA trajectory will achieve our guided objective of 2.8% - 3% exit Q4FY27. 
Before I move on to our progress on Lakshya 2031, I would like to take a few minutes to address a topic 
that many of you would have been tracking, and that is the consultation paper issued by Insurance 
Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) on insurance distribution and commission 
structures. 
As the framework is still a draft consultation paper, it would be premature to quantify the final impact. 
The paper proposes to rationalise the commission payouts across the board with significant cuts in 
credit-linked insurance and motor insurance. There is also a significant attenuation in the thresholds of 
commission payouts on standalone insurance products however, to a lesser extent. We understand 
that the regulators suggestion on the consultation paper are from a viewpoint of making insurance more 
affordable for the common man in line with the Government of India’s ‘Insurance for All’ as a part of the 
Viksit Bharat 2047 plan. We believe that there is significant scope for consultation with the regulator on 
creating an economic rationale for the BFSI entities to continue supporting the insurance industry 
through their distribution channels. It is to be noted that out of all the Credit Life insurance policies sold 
in the country, approximately 90%-95% are sold by Banks & NBFCs distribution channels. This touches 
65-85 Mn lives (source: Nomura Report estimates Jan’2026)  in the country annually and accounts for ~35% of all 
Insurance policies issued in India. As an industry, our SRO FIDC is working with all member NBFCs to 
kickstart an engagement with the regulator, possibly in collaboration with other financial industry SROs. 
The salient points of discussion would be a realistic assessment of the distribution costs incurred by the 
BFSI industry to support distribution of insurance products on behalf of the insurance manufacturer. We 
would also request the regulator for a glide path for commission optimisation to distributors in line with

the glide path proposed for the manufacturers in the treatment of expense of management (EoM). As 
an industry we would pursue all possible channels of dialogue to ensure that the final outcome is 
balanced and positive for all stakeholders - consumers, distributors, and manufacturers of insurance. 
As an organisation we will look at all possible means of revenue optimisation, including new initiatives 
like cross-sell as well as the Payments business focusing on value adding agentic commerce. In 
summary, we expect L&T Finance to navigate the IRDAI consultation paper related impact with minimal 
disruption to our Lakshya 2031 goals. 
We will also like to apprise you about two very important initiatives that we have started in Q2FY27, 
which we expect to gather pace over the next couple of quarters. 
The first is Project Hercules - our increased focus on reducing cost of customer acquisition through 
focused cross-sell initiatives to our existing customer base leveraging our extensive Agentic AI 
expertise. You may be aware that L&T Finance has one of the largest customer bases in the NBFC 
industry at 3 crore customers and an equally large number of prospects who have applied for products 
from the company at some point in time and were found to be not eligible at that instance. The fact that 
our Rural Group Loans and MFI customers, Tractor customers and Two-Wheeler customers have 
borrowed more than 50,000 Cr worth of gold loans prompted our entry into the gold loan business. To 
effectively tap into the demand of this large base of customers, an integrated agentic AI-based cross-
sell engine called Hercules is being built and implemented in phases. Q2FY27 saw the implementation 
of phase 1 of the Hercules cross-sell engine across a few important lines of business with promising 
initial results. For example, the conversion of gold loan cross-sell leads generated by other businesses 
is running at 14%+ as of the first week of October’26. The full complement of Hercules with the agentic 
AI workflows will be implemented by early December’26 and will be showcased to the investors during 
L&T Finance Investor Digital Day on 15th December’26. We expect the momentum of cross-sell volume 
build up to improve further in Q4FY27 and add to our low acquisition cost disbursement build-up in 
FY28. 
The second major initiative is our Payments platform which is being rapidly built to provide an agentic 
commerce experience to our customers and will also be a driver for increased new customer acquisition 
velocity. Our UPI stack is live and currently undergoing closed user group testing. We are implementing 
the agentic commerce payments stack in partnership with Pine Labs and we will unveil this effort at 
RAISE 2026. We have also applied for a Prepaid Issuer license, and we expect to bring a host of AI 
enabled prepaid payment products in FY28, subject to the receipt of the PPI license from RBI.

'Transformation' to 'Delivery’. 
I am pleased to state that we have begun this journey on a strong footing. While our profitability metrics 
continue to improve quarter after quarter, our immediate focus remains on maintaining consistency in 
execution. We recognize that Lakshya 2031 is a five-year journey and therefore, our endeavour remains

● 
Book growth - We had set ourselves a book growth CAGR of 20%+ over the Lakshya period, 
against which we have achieved a robust 28% growth in Q2FY27, supported by disbursement 
momentum across both secured and unsecured products: 72% YoY in Personal Loans, 24% 
YoY in Two-Wheeler Finance, 22% YoY in Rural Business Finance, 20% YoY in Mortgage 
Loans, 27% YoY in SME Finance and 9% YoY in Farmer Finance  
● 
Second, on the Credit Cost front, we continue to drive credit costs down to a level of 2% or 
less over the Lakshya period. In Q2FY27 our credit cost stood at 2.46%. Our participation in 
the Central Government's credit guarantee schemes, CGFMU and CGTMSE, continues to 
create an incremental safety net for select cohorts of our Rural Business Finance and SME 
Finance portfolios as outlined in slide no. 36 of our investor presentation. The continued 
moderation in credit costs and improving asset quality during the quarter provide us confidence 
that these structural interventions are delivering the intended outcomes. 
● 
Our Return on Assets (RoA) target remains in the range of 3.0%–3.2% for FY31. Against that, 
we recorded an RoA of 2.60% in Q2FY27, vs. 2.41% (after utilisation of macro prudential 
provisions) in the corresponding quarter in FY26, up 19 bps YoY. We remain committed to work 
on achieving the 2.8%-3.0% RoA corridor threshold in Q4FY27 as communicated earlier.  
● 
On Return on Equity (RoE) front against a Lakshya’31 target in the range of 16-18% by FY31, 
RoE increased to 13.56% in Q2FY27 from 11.31% (RoE after macro prudential provisions) in 
Q2FY26, up by 223bps.   
 
In my last call, I outlined our three key strategic objectives for FY27: Driving Cross-sell and Up-sell, 
Enhancing Productivity and Embedding a strong Tech-DNA across the organization. We continue to 
drive the key outcomes defined by these pillars, as they remain critical to achieving our short and long-
term business targets while building sustainable capabilities for future growth. 
While I have already spoken in detail about our cross-sell engine, Project Hercules, I want to highlight 
the momentum we are seeing in our other initiatives. Our second objective—driving organizational 
productivity—has gathered speed. We are actively enhancing productivity across all business lines, 
with a primary focus on empowering our frontline employees through customized performance 
dashboards. 
Thirdly, in line with our strategic objectives of embedding AI-empowered tools across the organization, 
we have made significant efforts to inculcate a "Tech DNA" throughout our workforce. As part of our 
initiative to upgrade the Tech DNA, LTF launched the "AI Citizen" program, equipping 1,200+ 
employees with the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and a continuous learning ecosystem with 
dedicated training sessions by industry experts. The goal here is to build custom agents that 
exponentially boost operational productivity. Following exclusive training, this initiative is rapidly 
expanding enterprise-wide to build a robust network of AI Champions, ensuring that AI is not just a 
central technology function, but a democratized tool actively used by our employees. It is worth

tasks have already been created by our employees. 
These strategic objectives are central to our structural evolution into a 'Risk-First, Tech-First' AI-native 
multi-product retail financier of choice. 
I will now request Mr. Raju Dodti, our Whole-Time Director and Chief Operating Officer, to take you

execution.

Central to our distribution strategy is the transformation of our legacy physical network to a multi-product

relationship management, enhancing customer lifetime value by positioning every branch as a gateway 
to our full suite of financial solutions. Specifically, as we have shared in previous quarters, we have
